A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FloodDiffusion and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–E. No material gaps prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanML3D and BABEL evaluations, ablations, hyperparameter experiments, and a 100-participant user study, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark, ablation, hyperparameter, and user-study results in Tables 1–6 and the qualitative figures.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same triangular schedule, bidirectional attention, frame-wise text conditioning, causal VAE, and training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D and BABEL for the same single-prompt and time-varying-prompt motion tasks. Qualitative test scenarios and user-study coverage also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the benchmark, VAE, and user-study comparisons, including PRIMAL and MotionStreamer. Changed citation numbers do not indicate different evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–E retain the same splits, 20 fps and 263-dimensional representation, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, baseline adaptations, and 100-participant study protocol.

E4.justification: The attention and scheduler ablations, VAE comparison, CFG sweep, architectural and inference-setting sweeps, and qualitative conditioning examples are unchanged in Tables 3–5 and Figures 4–6.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its 95% confidence-interval convention. Supplementary uncertainty reporting, raw user-study vote counts, and Bradley–Terry analysis are unchanged; no run or seed information is added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings remain unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports HumanML3D FID of 0.057 ± 0.002 and BABEL AUJ of 14.05 ± 0.663 for FloodDiffusion in both versions.

T1.justification: The vectorized dynamics, causal-dependency assumption, conditional-generation and streaming-locality results, and Appendix B proofs remain unchanged. The page 4 reflow does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, distribution-matching guarantee, streaming capability, and state-of-the-art performance claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations remain unchanged, including Section 4.3's limitations concerning semantic memory, commands referring to past motion, and unevaluated style shifting and long-term consistency.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, baseline modifications, and supplementary configurations are unchanged. Both versions provide the same project URL and code, model, and weight availability statement.

R1.justification: Reference [2] changes from Harold Benoit's diffusion-forcing web note to Chen et al.'s Diffusion Forcing research paper. The M2D2M and Video diffusion models with local-global context guidance references are removed. Broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects the unresolved 'Figure X' reference to 'Figure 3', updates the arXiv header, and revises numerous bibliographic details and citation numbers. Main prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from the upper-right to the upper-left column on page 4, reflowing the surrounding methods text. Reference pages also reflow; figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Replacing the diffusion-forcing web note with the research-paper citation improves attribution, and correcting 'Figure X' improves navigation. These are limited scholarly and editorial gains; the methods, proofs, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
